target_claim: The proof asserts that the configuration it just described (elements x1,y1,x2,y2 with z1 = x1∘y1, z2 = x2∘y2, z1 ≠ z2, ¬(z1=x1 ∧ z2=x2), ¬(z1=y1 ∧ z2=y2), for an operation ∘ that is none of the right/left/constant operations) can occur only when |S| > 3. This is false: an explicit 3-element set with an explicit operation table realizes all of the stated conditions, so the proof's cardinality claim (which would also wrongly exclude the |S| = 3 case allowed by the hypothesis "at least 3 elements") is refuted by a finite witness.
source_quote: The above are possible only if there are more than $3$ [[Definition:Element|elements]] in $S$.
